newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Gencor shares rise ahead of H1 results.
newsitem.headline: Gencor shares rise ahead of H1 results.

text.p: Shares in South African mining house Gencor Ltd rose sharply on Tuesday ahead of the release of its interim results later in the day.

At 1155 GMT the Gencor stock had risen 30 cents to trade at 19.80 rand -- just 20 cents shy of an annual high reached on January 17 this year -- on turnover of some 1.1 million shares valued at 21.9 million rand.
"I think this in in anticipation of good results. The market is looking for a good performance. I think the average consensus is about 35 percent up from the same period in 1995," one dealer said.
Analysts polled by Reuters expected Gencor to post increased earnings for the first half with strong contributions from its aluminium and coal interests.

Earnings per share were expected to rise from 48.5 cents in the six months to end-December 1995 to 64.1 cents in the latest period, while a dividend of 9.0 cents was forecast, up from the previous 7.0 cents a year ago.
Dealers said although the market was generally expecting good results, they could not discount the possibility of a leak pushing the stock higher.
They noted that the counter had also traded heavily overnight.
"The majority of business that went through was overnight purchases...There was just some good volume traded in the market," one said.
Gencor's results will be released at 1400 GMT.
